evidence: The crystallinity of MoO3 nano-ﬁlms was also studied by the microRaman spectroscopy (HORIBA, Lab Ram ARAMIS) with excitation source of λ = 532 nm of argon-ion laser with beam diameter spot of 2μm. The FTIR spectra of the as-deposited MoO3 nano-ﬁlms were taken and studied by using FTIR model Nicolet IS-5 spectrometer. The surface characterization of the ALD developed MoO3 nano-ﬁlms was performed by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) by Thermo Scientiﬁc Theta Probe XPS. The surface morphology of the ALD-fabricated MoO3 nano-ﬁlms (250 °C) is presented in Fig. 8(b) accompanied by its high magniﬁcation image. The AFM was used to investigate both the surface morphology and thickness of the developed nano-ﬁlms. After ALD process, the wafers were diced into 1.0 × 1.0 cm samples (Dynatex DTX, U.S.) for further material characterization. The ﬁeld emission scanning electron microscope (FE-SEM, JEOL 7800F) and atomic force microscope (AFM) (JPK system Nano wizard) were employed to investigate the surface morphology of MoO3 nano-ﬁlms. The variable angle in-situ spectroscopic ellipsometry measurements (J.A. Woollam M2000 DI) were carried out at the different incident angles (60°, 65°, 70°, 75°) over the wavelengths of 250– 1690 nm to monitor the uniformity and to measure the thickness of the deposited MoO3 ﬁlms.
